16:35 Local Time, 12:35 GMT, 18:05 IST: Not a single session in this Test gave us the feeling that a definite result was on the cards. A draw seemed inevitable for the better part of five days, and that's exactly how it panned out. Zimbabwe, after opting to bat, piled up 504 in their first innings, and things could have taken an interesting turn had they held on to the chances off the first two balls of their bowling innings. They didn't, and Sediqullah Atal made them pay with a fighting 105. Zimbabwe then had to contend with Rahmat Shah's immense grit and resilience for the best part of Days 3 and 4. By the time they walked out to bat in their second innings, the result was pretty much a foregone conclusion, and their batters made the most of the opportunity to get some valuable time in the middle ahead of the second Test.

It has been a nightmare of a game for the bowlers, with the surface offering very little assistance. The pacers found some movement with the new ball, but the spinners had to rely largely on mistakes from the batters on an extremely slow pitch with hardly any variation in bounce. The batters, meanwhile, had a field day, with Brendan Taylor, Brian Bennett, Sediqullah Atal, Rahmanullah Zadran, Rahmat Shah, Craig Ervine and Wessly Madhevere among the biggest beneficiaries. Ervine, in particular, made Afghanistan pay dearly for their missed opportunities, after being dropped twice by Rahmat Shah, on nought and 162, before going on to register his maiden Test double-century. From Zimbabwe's perspective, a fifty on debut for Antum Naqvi and a maiden five-wicket haul for Newman Nyamhuri will provide plenty of encouragement heading into the next game. All in all a forgettable contest for the bowlers. Stick around for the post match reactions...

Rahmat Shah | Afghanistan skipper: [On scoring another hundred and assessing the batting conditions] I'm very happy. I love my batting. Assess the condition early and just use the feet movement as well and just play on the straight bat. [On his previous success against Zimbabwe] I think the second Test in Bulawayo. That was one my good moment against Zimbabwe. I think I scored 139. And that match we won. [On the performances of Sediqullah Atal and the debutant Rahmanullah Zadran] Yeah, Zadran is a good talent. He performed well in the domestic cricket. I hope he continues this in the next match. [On formulating plans in the middle and Saleem Safi's bowling] Yeah, Safi is a good hard worker, good hard working bowler. According the plan he bowl always. And I hope he continue this form and this bowling in the next match.

A rather dull draw after five days of hard grind, but will things be any different in the second Test? The good news is that the teams will move to a different surface, one that is currently being watered, and hopefully offers something more for the bowlers when the two sides meet again on Friday. Same venue, same time, but expect both teams to consider bringing in an extra bowling option to improve their chances of forcing a result. Here's hoping we get a more competitive contest with something in it for everyone. Do join us for the second Test. Until then, cheers and goodbye!!
